correctness.rationale: The exact two-vertex equations are transformed into mean, contrast and chemical modes. A strictly increasing two-parameter artanh representation gives G_t<0 on the asymmetric branch. The linearization splits off eigenvalue −beta, and its remaining characteristic cubic has A,B,C>0 and AB−C>0 because 0<q<e and D=−r eta G_t/2>0. Algebraic identities were checked symbolically, the matrix was checked against direct finite differences, and 164 positive-parameter recovered equilibria passed independent finite spectral consistency checks. Finite checks corroborate rather than prove the all-parameter theorem; only strict positive rates and finite chi>threshold are claimed.

originality.rationale: The closest primary source and previously available exact two-vertex equilibrium census establish the homogeneous instability threshold and existence and monotonicity of patterned states but do not establish their all-rate four-dimensional spectral stability. Database queries and PDE comparisons found no stronger applicable result, although historical priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The natural dynamical question left unresolved by a complete patterned-state census is whether chemotaxis can cause secondary Hopf or other instabilities. An all-parameter exclusion of every local patterned-state instability in a nonlinear four-dimensional feedback model is a structural theorem, not a routine special value or a repetition of stationary enumeration; it remains nontrivial across the regime where a cross-derivative reverses sign. The result is a benchmark stability diagram, not a claim about global attraction.
